title: Clinical trial Phase III to study whether magnesium sulfate improves nerve block in knee surgeries.
official: Phase III Randomized, Double-Blind Clinical Trial to Determine the Role of Magnesium Sulfate in Adductor Canal Block in Total Knee Arthroplasty
summary: Main objective: Evaluate the efficacy of perineural magnesium sulfate in prolonging analgesia when administered as an adjuvant to the local anesthetic ropivacaine in total knee arthroplasty.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients scheduled for total knee arthroplasty due to gonarthrosis
2. ASA I, II, and III patients of both sexes.
3. Age between 18 and 80 years.
4. Informed consent signed, accepting participation in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Allergy or intolerance to local anesthetics, morphine or its derivatives, magnesium sulfate.
2. Patients with any condition that prevents the use of regional analgesia: anticoagulated, antiplatelet therapy, local or systemic infection.
3. Patients with difficulty understanding study-related information and collaborating in pain assessment.
4. Patients with major psychiatric pathology as per DSM-V.
5. Pregnancy and/or breastfeeding.
6. ASA IV Patients
7. Diabetes mellitus with the last glycated hemoglobin control greater than 7%.
8. Patients with neuromuscular diseases.
9. Morbid obesity.
10. Fibromyalgia
11. Myofascial pain syndrome.
12. Patients with prior treatment with corticosteroids or calcium antagonists in the last three months.
13. Patients with cardiovascular disease (congestive heart failure, severe valvular disease, symptomatic coronary artery disease, and/or congenital/anatomical heart abnormalities).
14. Patients with severe renal, hepatic, or respiratory disease.
